cards.explanation: The answer is righteousness, friends. John says, "With righteousness He judges and wages war." (Revelation 19:11) Righteousness is the way He judges and the way He wages war. I can't say the same about my first batch of the morning.

The answer is True, friends. John says, "He has a name written on Him that only He Himself knows." (Revelation 19:12) So there's a name on Him that only He knows. I have "Dorin" carved in my handle, and that one is no secret.
The answer is False, friends. The armies of heaven "…follow Him on white horses." (Revelation 19:14) They ride behind the rider, not ahead of Him. So He is in front and they come behind Him.

The answer is fine linen, white and pure, friends. John says they are "…dressed in fine linen, white and pure…" (Revelation 19:14) They follow the rider on white horses in that clothing. White clothes on white horses, and I'd be nervous bringing my flour-dusted apron anywhere near that parade.
The answer is nations, friends. The sword is "…with which to strike down the nations…" (Revelation 19:15) John says it proceeds from His mouth. So the nations are who the sword is for.

The answer is God the Almighty, friends. John says, "He treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God the Almighty." (Revelation 19:15) So the wrath belongs to God the Almighty. It's a heavy line, and I think it's worth slowing down for.

The answer is KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS, friends! John says, "…He has a name written on His robe and on His thigh: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS." (Revelation 19:16) Many crowns on His head, and a name like that on His robe. It all fits.

The answer is the birds flying overhead, friends. The angel "…cried out in a loud voice to all the birds flying overhead…" (Revelation 19:17) So his message goes to the birds. He is calling them to gather for what he names the great supper of God.

The answer is False, friends. The angel's list goes on past kings, commanders and mighty men to "…horses and riders, of everyone slave and free, small and great." (Revelation 19:18) So the list doesn't stop where the question says it does. It reaches well past the kings, commanders and mighty men.

The answer is the rider and His army, friends. John sees the beast and the kings of the earth assembled "…to wage war against the One seated on the horse, and against His army." (Revelation 19:19) So they're facing the rider and His army. I wouldn't want to be on that side of the field.

The answer is True, friends. John says, "…the beast was captured along with the false prophet…" (Revelation 19:20) The beast gathers for war against the rider, and it ends up captured. That is a heavy part of the passage, and I think it's okay to feel it.

The answer is that he performed signs that deceived people, friends. John says the false prophet, "…on its behalf had performed signs deceiving those who had the mark of the beast and worshiped its image." (Revelation 19:20) So he used signs to deceive people. I think this one is heavy.
